components.summary: Use Button when one clear action moves someone forward, confirms a choice, or completes a task.
Use a Text Input for a single line of text, such as a search, with an icon that hints at what to type.
Use a Badge to make a short status, category, or count easy to scan beside the content it describes.
Reveal supporting details when people need them, while keeping the page easy to scan.
Use Stack when a public component slot needs one token-driven gap and an intentional vertical or horizontal direction.
Use a Benefit Card to list what a plan or offer gives, with an optional upsell and one button to upgrade.
Use VStack for page flow, grouped details, and ordered content. Its children follow token-driven spacing and padding while the host supplies the available height.
Use HStack for a row of related content. It owns horizontal rhythm, alignment, and optional wrapping while the host decides how much room the row has.
Keep a few related actions in one row with shared spacing and modes.
Use an Icon Button for a frequent, well-known action where an icon alone is clear, such as add, share, or close.
Use a Link to send people to related content, such as terms, help, or a recovery step, on its own line or inside a sentence.
Use a Form Field to collect one labelled value, such as an account number, with a hint or an error message below it.
Use Checkbox Item for a selectable row with a clear label and, when needed, a supporting action.
Use Tabs to switch between a few peer views of the same content, such as an account’s overview, activity, and details.
Use a Tab Item inside Tabs for each view: a short label that turns black with a gold underline while its view is showing.
Use a Nudge for a short suggestion with one action, such as splitting a payment, that sits within a screen’s content.
Keep page identity, navigation and a few relevant actions together at the top of a view.
Keep the next step close to the decision.
Use a Stepper to show where someone is in a process with several stages, such as KYC, and how each stage went.
Use a Step for one stage of a process inside a Stepper, such as Verify PAN, with its number or outcome and a line of detail.
Use a Slider to pick a value from a wide range by dragging, such as a monthly SIP amount or a loan tenure.
